items.text: Isaiah had a unique gift for expressing God’s word in vivid, memorable language. His teachings transcend his own generation, offering profound truths about God’s great work of redemption that apply to all people and all times, inspiring prophets for centuries.

The Savior taught that “all things that [Isaiah] spake have been and shall be, even according to the words which he spake.” Studying Isaiah can reveal prophecies with multiple fulfillments, from his day to the Savior's mortal ministry and the latter days.

President Dallin H. Oaks stated that Isaiah’s prophecies often have multiple meanings, applying to Isaiah's day, the Savior's time, and the events of the Second Coming. Seeking revelation from the Holy Ghost is crucial for interpreting these profound messages.

To understand Isaiah, ponder his symbols and metaphors. Ask, “What am I learning about Jesus Christ?” Look for topics relevant to our time and use study helps. The Savior declared, “Search these things diligently; for great are the words of Isaiah.”

Like prophets throughout history, Isaiah warned people about their spiritual condition and the consequences of sin. He also offered messages of hope for redemption through the Savior, revealing the Lord’s power to overcome wickedness and restore His people.

Prophets today, like Isaiah, warn us about sin and its destructive consequences. They also offer powerful messages of hope through Jesus Christ, reminding us that through Him, we can overcome challenges and find redemption. Consider recent general conference messages.

Isaiah prophesied of a great work God would accomplish in the latter days. By looking for future-tense verbs in chapters like Isaiah 2, 4, 11, and 12, we can discover inspiring prophecies about Zion, temple building, and the gathering of Israel.

The prophecy in Isaiah 2:2–3, speaking of the mountain of the Lord being exalted and all nations flowing unto it, is particularly relevant for Latter-day Saints. It points to the establishment of God’s kingdom on the earth in the latter days.

Isaiah’s words provide assurance that God’s promises will be fulfilled. Even when people stray, the Lord’s power to save and redeem remains. His covenant people will ultimately be gathered and blessed, and His kingdom will be established.

The Book of Isaiah is quoted frequently by other scriptures, including by Jesus Christ Himself. This highlights the profound doctrinal truths and prophetic insights contained within its pages, making it a vital resource for understanding God’s plan.
